title: Grace! 'Tis a Charming Sound
description: Grace! 'Tis a Charming Sound in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 652 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Grace first and last in Salvation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Grace! 'tis a charm-ing sound! Har-mo-nious to the ear! Hea-ven with th'e-cho shall re-sound, And all the earth shall hear.

lines: Heaven with the echo shall resound,
And all the earth shall hear.
And all the steps that grace display
And new supplies each hour I meet
Grace taught my soul to pray,
'Twas grace that kept me to this day,
And will not let me go.
Grace all the work shall crown,
It lays in heaven the topmost stone,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
